Tiszalok Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tiszalök, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Tiszalök in the early 18th century - one family by 1736 - growing to 53 by 1784 and peaking at 556 around 1880, before declining to 362 by 1941. A synagogue was built in 1840 and a school in 1878; the community affiliated with the Orthodox stream in 1867. Seventeen Tiszalök Jews died in World War I, and the community endured pogroms during the 1919-21 'White Terror.' Forty young men died during forced labor conscription in 1941. After Germany's 1944 occupation, the town's rabbi - who also worked as the butcher - was arrested and beaten; following Passover, all of Tiszalök's Jews were gathered in the synagogue and taken by cart to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto, then deported to Auschwitz by freight train on May 23. Only 15 survivors returned after the war, and hostility from local residents prevented them from re-establishing the community. The cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1850, its newest to 1936.
